Digests in the Style of openssl

Source: R/digest-mirror.R
crypt_sha.Rd

crypt_sha1(), crypt_sha256(), crypt_sha384() and crypt_sha512() mirror openssl::sha1() and its siblings for raw input: the digest, or with key the HMAC, as a raw vector of class c("hash", "<algorithm>"), and "hmac" after them for an HMAC. They exist first so that crypt_signature_create() can take hash = crypt_sha256 as openssl::signature_create() takes hash = sha256.

This version accepts raw vectors only. openssl also hashes character vectors element-wise and reads connections; that typing, and the other digests, arrive with the rest of the openssl-shaped layer.

crypt_sha1() is for formats that specify SHA-1. It is not collision resistant; use crypt_sha256() for anything new.

Usage

crypt_sha1(x, key = NULL)

crypt_sha256(x, key = NULL)

crypt_sha384(x, key = NULL)

crypt_sha512(x, key = NULL)

Arguments

x

A raw vector.

key

NULL for a digest, or a raw key for an HMAC.

Value

A raw vector of class c("hash", "<algorithm>"): 20, 32, 48 or 64 bytes.

See also

crypt_hash() and crypt_hmac(), the core functions these wrap.

Examples

crypt_sha256(charToRaw("abc"))
#> sha256 ba:78:16:bf:8f:01:cf:ea:41:41:40:de:5d:ae:22:23:b0:03:61:a3:96:17:7a:9c:b4:10:ff:61:f2:00:15:ad 
crypt_sha256(charToRaw("abc"), key = charToRaw("secret"))
#> sha256 hmac 99:46:da:d4:e0:0e:91:3f:c8:be:8e:5d:3f:7e:11:0a:4a:9e:83:2f:83:fb:09:c3:45:28:5d:78:63:8d:8a:0e
